title: Harden catalog contract fallback and repair regressed export
summary: Protect the Vault against malformed catalog exports and restore the lyrics-era export contract when GCS drifts.

Resolved on 2026-04-08 by fixing the Cloud Run fallback path to use the baked dist/catalog.csv snapshot, redeploying suno-viewer, and republishing the repaired latest_catalog_wide.csv plus metadata to GCS. Control Center now reports both GCS and fallback healthy, and the live catalog contract again includes the lyrics/styles-era fields.

title: Validate export contract before publish and before serve
summary: Define required catalog.csv columns and fail both export and serving paths when required fields disappear unexpectedly.
notes: This is the first active prevention ticket under EPIC-18. It should make catalog contract drift explicit instead of silent by validating required columns in the export producer path and keeping the viewer-side schema guard as a second consumer-side gate.

title: Expose export health and fallback state in the Control Center
summary: Show whether the Vault is serving from GCS or fallback, required-column health, missing fields, and export freshness in the Control Center.
notes: Moved to In Progress on 2026-04-08. /api/admin/overview now returns catalog health inspection data and the Control Center renders serving source, GCS vs fallback health, and missing required columns so contract drift is visible before it becomes a user-reported Vault regression.

title: Add post-deploy smoke validation for Vault runtime integrity
summary: Define and run minimum live checks after deploy so the Vault is not treated as healthy until catalog, lyrics, styles, auth, and publish gating still work.
notes: This ticket closes the gap between deploy success and product reality by requiring a small set of live runtime checks after releases that touch viewer, export, auth, or queue-adjacent surfaces.

title: Split daily health reporting into subsystem health
summary: Separate harvest, export contract, viewer, queue, caption, and auth/admin health so one green pipeline email does not mask a degraded product surface.
notes: The goal is to stop treating a single pipeline-healthy signal as sufficient when the live Vault feed or admin surfaces can still be degraded.

title: Standardize incident and postmortem capture for regressions
summary: Create one repeatable regression incident template covering symptom, impact, trigger, escape reason, immediate fix, and prevention follow-up.
notes: This keeps future regressions from dissolving into scattered notes by forcing a single operational memory format with linked fixes and prevention tickets.

title: Enforce single active Vault player
summary: Ensure starting playback on one song stops any other active Vault player so overlapping audio cannot happen.
notes: Current Vault cards can play multiple songs at the same time. Expected behavior is one active player globally: playing a new song should stop the currently playing song and transfer active playback state.

summary: Switch canonical product-facing domains to Sundrop and preserve legacy domain access through redirects during the transition window.
notes: This should only happen after dual-domain validation is clean and should include close monitoring of auth, export, queue, email, and publishing behavior.

title: Add YouTube API quota guardrails and quota-safe call strategy
summary: Prevent quota traps by budgeting YouTube API usage, preferring quota-cheap read paths, consolidating writes, and exposing quota risk before bulk publish or metadata operations.
notes: Opened on 2026-04-14 from standup planning. This ticket should document the real quota-cost hotspots, replace avoidable search.list usage with cheaper playlist/list patterns where possible, batch metadata writes into single update calls, add retry/backoff rules that do not accidentally multiply expensive requests, and surface enough quota context that operators can plan uploads and bulk edits without guessing.

title: Plan post-beta Vault serving transition away from CSV-primary
summary: Keep CSV as a beta-era export/fallback artifact, but define the transition to an authenticated API-backed Vault read model so stale snapshots stop being a primary product risk.
notes: Opened on 2026-04-14. The current CSV model is still useful during beta because it keeps troubleshooting relatively simple, but it is also a recurring break point for freshness, fallback precedence, and access-model drift. This ticket should define a post-beta transition where CSV remains an export/fallback layer while live Vault reads move to an auth-aware typed API or server-side read model.

title: Add Vault diagnostic toolbox with operator-run checks and one-click common fixes
summary: Add a lightweight operator toolbox near Queue Inspector that can run Vault health checks, show a concise report, and trigger safe first-line fixes for the most common catalog and media failures.
notes: Opened on 2026-04-14. This is the near-term stabilization move that should help during beta without bogging down product progress. The toolbox should check freshness, serving source, export contract health, media/lyrics availability, and queue/publish readiness, then offer a small set of clearly labeled fix actions such as refresh export source, republish latest catalog artifact, or rebuild fallback snapshot.

title: Harden Vault auth storage and move privileged sessions toward HttpOnly cookies
summary: Keep the beta-friendly Firebase SPA flow working, but define and implement the safer next step where operator and other privileged sessions stop depending on browser-readable local auth state.
notes: Opened on 2026-04-14 after reviewing Firebase auth state in browser storage during Vault debugging. This should not block beta momentum, but it should become the main hardening lane for admin/operator access. The work should audit all current localStorage/sessionStorage auth usage, introduce a server-issued HttpOnly session-cookie path for privileged surfaces, and leave only low-risk UI state in browser storage.

title: Eliminate protected media URL leakage and repeated 401 thumb noise
summary: Stop publishing raw protected /api/song-media URLs into the Vault DOM where the browser can speculative-fetch them without auth, generating noisy 401s and avoidable protected-media exposure patterns.
notes: Opened on 2026-04-14 after live Vault debugging showed authenticated pages rendering correctly while the console filled with unauthorized thumb requests. Completed on 2026-04-14 by routing protected thumbnail/open-artwork links through the authenticated blob/object-URL path instead of exposing raw /api/song-media URLs in the DOM, which cleared the repeated thumb 401 console flood while preserving protected media delivery.

title: Reduce Vault startup session latency and critical-request chaining
summary: Shorten the initial /vault startup chain by reducing duplicate session work, improving session endpoint latency, and trimming avoidable render-blocking and startup-layout cost without destabilizing beta debugging.
notes: Opened on 2026-04-14 from live DevTools traces during Vault crash and recovery work. The page is currently usable, but startup still pays heavily for api/auth/session, duplicate auth/session resolution, and some first-render layout work. Moved to In Progress on 2026-04-14 after the auth bootstrap was tightened to wait for Firebase token resolution before loading /api/auth/session, a low-risk preconnect hint was added for identitytoolkit.googleapis.com, the first catalog fetch was switched to reuse the already-resolved auth token, the Vault catalog load effect was narrowed to real browse-access signals instead of the whole session object, protected auth-control mutations were switched to reuse the resolved token, stale startup session/catalog requests were made abortable, the server-side metadata access token used by the session path was cached in-process until near expiry, and session timing instrumentation was added for future authenticated trace analysis. A fresh unauthenticated browser trace now shows a single /api/auth/session request on startup. Quick public-route verification did not surface the new timing headers or opt-in debug payload yet, so the next pass should verify how those values behave through the full hosting path before relying on them. Remaining work should verify the authenticated trace path and then profile the next safe startup/layout reductions.

Remaining work should harden long-running export durability, refine tier gating, and add operator/customer-friendly export history and recovery UX.

title: Improve Vault retrieval and search
summary: Turn Vault search into a real retrieval surface with richer matching, structured filters, saved views, and search-to-action workflows.

This epic owns discoverability, narrowing, saved retrieval views, and workflow-aware search for Vault, publishing, and operator use. summary: Translate the Vault into a true mobile-first browse surface with compact relic rows, status-forward hierarchy, bottom navigation, and creator-safe controls without introducing a separate mobile URL.

This ticket owns the responsive mobile version of the main Vault browse experience on the existing /vault route, including the compact list presentation, mobile header, account context, filter affordances, and lower-page machine status block.

title: Add Sovereign Catalog mobile view with dense list controls
summary: Create the mobile version of the condensed Sovereign Catalog view with metadata-first rows, publish actions, pagination, and per-page item count controls.
notes: Opened on 2026-04-12 alongside the desktop Sovereign Catalog concept. This ticket covers the mobile behavior for the condensed catalog list, including at least 50-item paging support, mobile-safe action density, and a route/query model that stays under the existing Vault surface instead of creating a duplicate app.

title: Implement mobile publish and release configuration flow
summary: Turn publish into a mobile-first release configuration flow with selected-song context, title override, playlist targeting, description template controls, privacy selection, and clear approval-safe actions.
notes: Opened on 2026-04-12 from the approved Release Configuration mobile reference. This ticket owns the handheld publish surface for Tier 3 users/operators, whether implemented as a full-screen route, sheet, or drawer, as long as it preserves the existing Vault source truth and only edits publish-layer fields.

title: Define shared mobile navigation and action patterns for Vault surfaces
summary: Standardize the mobile header, bottom navigation, menu behavior, and action placement across Vault browse, Sovereign Catalog, and publish so the mobile experience feels like one coherent product.
notes: Opened on 2026-04-12 to keep mobile Vault work coherent instead of page-by-page improvisation. This ticket should define which controls are global, which are admin-only, and how browse, catalog, and publish states share one recognizable mobile shell.

title: Track edge cases and production anomalies
summary: Create a real home for malformed data, runtime oddities, import anomalies, and product edge cases that are too important to lose but too cross-cutting to force into a single lane.
notes: Opened on 2026-04-10. This epic owns weird-but-real production behavior such as malformed Vault imports, stale media fallbacks, partial enrichments, and customer-visible anomalies that need tracking even when they span harvest, Vault UI, auth, and media handling.

title: Define minimum viable song thresholds across import, Vault, and publish
summary: Define how incomplete a song record can be before harvest should reject it, Vault should hide it, or publish should block it, and then apply those rules consistently.
notes: Opened on 2026-04-10 from the malformed gravitystruth Vault row. This ticket is not about one song only; it owns the minimum viable song rule set. It should answer which fields are required for import acceptance, which are required for Vault display, which are required for playback, and which are required before a song can be queued or published.

title: Serve private song media without stale public fallback behavior
summary: Define and implement the correct behavior when artwork or audio exists only as private gs:// media so the Vault uses guarded app delivery instead of stale or incorrect public CDN guesses.
notes: Opened on 2026-04-10 from the gravitystruth artwork and audio mismatch. This ticket covers private-media proxying, fallback order, and when the Vault should show media-unavailable versus silently displaying the wrong artwork or audio.
